en: The Ritual for Bestowing Food, Drink, and Water upon Pretas, together with the Hand Gestures (Mudrās),
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Da Xingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom,
who was specially promoted to the rank of Court Commissioner for State Ceremonial (Honglu Qing) by imperial decree.
First, prepare food for sentient beings;
this must be done in accordance with the Dharma.
All varieties surrounding it should be attached [to the vessel], and everything must be pure and excellent.
Whether it be a portion, a small amount, or a single vessel,
all must be placed within a clean copper vessel according to the Dharma;
if no copper vessel is available, white porcelain is also acceptable.
Just as one may not use earthenware vessels, one may instead use lacquered vessels.
One's food and drink must be mixed with pure water.
One may perform the ritual while standing or sitting, facing east.
Now, those who wish to bestow food and drink upon all hungry ghosts must first give rise to a vast and great mind and universally invite the hungry ghosts;
they should first recite this verse once with a sincere heart.
Thereafter, perform the rite of invocation.
The merit and karmic rewards obtained thereby are beyond measure.
[Name], a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī, has resolved to uphold this with a single vessel of pure food.
Universally bestowing upon the ten directions, exhausting the entirety of empty space,
throughout all lands within the atoms of the Dharma-realm— whether they be all the realms of hungry ghosts,
the long-deceased ancestors of antiquity, the local spirits of mountains and rivers, or even those of the wilderness.
All you ghosts and spirits, please come and assemble here.
Out of compassion for you, I now bestow this food upon you all.
May you each receive this food of mine and, in turn, offer it throughout the entirety of space to the Buddhas and the Noble Ones.
May all sentient beings, you, and every living creature be fully satiated.
Furthermore, may your body, by virtue of this mantra-food, be freed from suffering and liberated,
reborn in heaven to enjoy bliss, and travel at will to the pure lands of the ten directions.
Having resolved to attain Bodhicitta and practicing the path of Bodhi, may you become Buddhas in the future and never regress.
To those who have previously attained the Way, I vow to deliver them all.
Furthermore, I pray that you will always protect me, day and night.
Fulfill my aspirations; I pray that you grant me this food.
Whatever merit is produced, I universally dedicate it for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm.
May it be shared equally with all sentient beings, and together with all sentient beings, may we collectively take hold of this merit.
Dedicating it all toward the *tathatā* dharma-realm, toward unsurpassed bodhi, and toward the knowledge of all-knowledge;
may I swiftly attain Buddhahood and not invite any other fruit.
May I rely upon this Dharma and quickly achieve Buddhahood.
Place the palms together at the heart and recite this verse.
To perform the mudrā of invocation, form the mudrā of opening the throat: with the right hand, join the thumb and middle finger face-to-face.
The remaining three fingers are spaced apart and slightly curved;
this is the seal known as the Seal of Universal Gathering (*Samantāgata-mudrā*). The mantra is as follows:
*Namo bhū-pu-ri-kā-ri-ta-ri-ta-thā-ga-ta-ya*. Recite this mantra seven times while forming this mudrā.
Extending vast compassion,
I vow that all hungry ghosts within every atom of the dharma-realm shall gather together like clouds.
Furthermore, recite the mantra for opening the gates of hell and the throat, which is:
Oṃ bhu bu ti ri ka ta ri ta tha ga ta ya. When reciting this mantra:
Holding the food vessel with the left hand,
form the mudrā of prior invocation with the right hand;
simply alter this by reciting the mantra once for each snap of the fingers.
Press the tips of the thumb and middle finger together;
snapping the fingers to make a sound is the [action].
Slightly open and bend the remaining three fingers; this is called the seal for breaking through the gates of hell and opening the throat.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke this *dhāraṇī* for sustaining food and drink through the power of immeasurable majestic virtue, sovereign radiance,
and supreme excellence: Namaḥ sarvātathāgatavaroṣitāya | Oṃ sara sara vara vara hūṃ || Recite this mantra seven times.
All the hungry ghosts each received seventy-seven *dronas* of food, measured by the *droṇa* used in the kingdom of Magadha;
having eaten, they were all reborn in the heavens or in pure lands.
It can cause the practitioner’s karmic obstructions to be eliminated and their lifespan to be increased;
they will obtain immeasurable and boundless merit in the present life,
let alone in future lives.
Then, forming the hand-seal and reciting this mantra, one consecrates the food and drink;
with the thumb of the right hand,
one rubs the nail of the middle finger two or three times.
Straighten the three fingers upright;
then, with the thumb pressing against the index finger,
snap the fingers to produce a sound.
Recite the mantra once and snap the fingers once;
this is it. Furthermore, recite the *Amṛtadharmarasamantra* while forming the *Abhayamudrā*.
Raise the right arm vertically,
extend the five fingers straight upward, and that is it.
The mantra is as follows:
Namaḥ surupāyatātathāgatāya tadyathā | oṃ suru suru prasu ru prasu ru svāhā. [Perform the previously mentioned mudrā of granting fearlessness.]
Recite this mantra, the Mantra for Bestowing Ambrosia,
seventeen times; it can cause food, drink,
and water to be transformed into immeasurable milk and ambrosia.
It is able to open the throats of all hungry ghosts,
enabling them to obtain food and drink in great abundance and to consume it equally.
Next, perform the visualization and mantra-seal of the One-Syllable Heart-Water Wheel of Vairocana.
First, visualize the syllable *vaṃ* within the palm of the right hand,
white like the color of milk,
which transforms into the ocean of eight meritorious qualities.
It causes all ambrosial *sarpis* (clarified butter) to flow forth.
Then, extending the hand over the food vessel, one recites the mantra,
chanting this syllable *VAṂ* seven times.
Then, extend the five fingers and lower them toward the vessel containing the food;
visualize the milk and other substances flowing forth from the syllables.
Just as the sun, the moon,
and the ocean of milk satisfy all hungry ghosts (preta) so that none lack anything,
this is called the Seal and Mantra for Universal Bestowal upon All Hungry Ghosts. It is said:
*Namo samantabuddhānām vaṃ*. Having visualized this and recited this mantra seven times, [one should proceed].
Write it on a pure ground where no people pass,
or by the side of a pond or beneath a tree; however,
one must not write it beneath peach trees, willow trees, or pomegranate trees.
Having finished writing this, recite the names of the five Tathāgatas three times with utmost sincerity; the merit is immeasurable.

Namaḥ samantabhadraya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Homage to the Tathāgata Samantabhadra, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One. This removes the karma of stinginess and greed, and brings the perfection of merit and virtue.
Namo bhagavate suvarṇavarṇāya tathāgatāya | Homage to the Tathāgata of Wondrous Golden Form, who has destroyed all unseemly appearances and whose marks and signs are perfectly complete.
Namaḥ bhagavate amṛtāyate rājāya tathāgatāya. Through this empowerment of the Amṛtarāja Tathāgata, may the body and mind receive bliss.
Namo bhagavate vipulakāya-svādita-rasāya tathāgatāya. Homage to the Tathāgata of Vast Body, whose throat is wide and who experiences exquisite flavors.
Namaḥ bhagavate aparājitāya tathāgatāya sarvabhayavigate sarvapretagatipariśuddhaye.
If a practitioner can act in this way and invoke the names of the five Tathāgatas,
they shall be graced by the majestic power and light of the Buddhas.
It can cause all hungry ghosts and others to extinguish immeasurable sins and generate immeasurable merit;
they shall obtain exquisite and expansive physical forms, attain fearlessness, and receive food and drink.
It shall be transformed into delicious food of ambrosia;
one will swiftly leave this body of suffering and be reborn in the pure land of heaven.
Once the food has been offered, [recite:]...
The practitioner should further recite for the sake of the various spirits and ghosts the Bodhisattva Samaya-sīla Dhāraṇī.
Each time one recites it three times, the mantra is as follows: [join the palms in the mudrā].
Oṃ samayas tvaṃ. Having recited this three times, all ghosts and spirits became capable of hearing the profound and secret Dharma.
Having fully attained the samaya precepts, one obtains immeasurable merit.
Once all the hungry ghosts have been completely satisfied by the offerings,
they must be dismissed according to the dharani ritual.
Only then may they return to their original abodes.
The mantra for dispatching and liberation is as follows:
Oṃ vajramukha kṣi muḥ. Recite this dispatching mantra.
First, perform the mantra-seal (mudrā):
form a fist with the right hand and press the tip of the index finger with the thumb.
Turn the palms upward and snap the fingers to make a sound;
this is called "Dispatching and Informing.
Whenever one has finished writing out the food offerings, recite [the mantra] seven times and snap the fingers.
It shall cause all ghosts and spirits to depart once they have received this food;
if it is not dismissed, they will not depart.
If one does not fully possess such qualities,
then when making offerings to the hungry ghosts (preta),
they will not be able to partake of them in their entirety; some may receive them, while others may not.
To labor in vain is truly deeply pitiable.
If there are practitioners who have resolved their minds on Bodhi and are able to practice in this manner, [they shall not suffer such loss].
When those who possess this Dharma bestow it upon the hungry ghosts (preta),
all hungry ghosts shall attain full satiation without any deficiency;
those who uphold the Dharma should know this entirely.
If one uses the *āhāra-adhiṣṭhāna-dhāraṇī* (the dhāraṇī for blessing food) to take a vessel of pure food and pour it into clear flowing water,
it will enable all brāhmaṇas and ṛṣis to obtain this food; having eaten, they shall all, with one voice and in unison, offer prayers of blessing.
This person shall attain longevity in this very life.
Possessing the majestic virtue of the Brahmā heavens, they shall practice the conduct of the Brahmā heavens.
If one uses this mantra to consecrate all offerings made to the Buddha, [the merit shall be immeasurable].
Whether it be water, incense, flowers, food, or drink,
one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over each and offer them as an oblation to the Buddha.
In this way, these various [practices] are no different from making offerings to all the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Regarding the bestowing of [offerings] upon the "Scorched-Face" (*Jiaomian*) hungry ghosts and all spirits and deities, there is a distinct essential decision (*yaojue*) concerning the *Dharani Sutra*, namely the *Jiumiannagui tuoluonijing* (Sutra of the Dharani for Saving the Scorched-Face Hungry Ghosts), translated by Shikshananda during the Tang dynasty.
Revised once more.
On the twenty-second day of the tenth month, the Venerable Teaching was revised once by Seijaku.
